conflicts.permit: We may tie your personal information, and your purchasing history, to information in the profile, in order to provide tailored promotions and marketing offers and to improve the content of the Site for you.
conflicts.prohibit: The use of a cookie is in no way linked to any Personal Information while on the Site.
conflicts.situation: Brookshire builds a preference profile from cookie data collected on the Site and ties a registered shopper's name and purchase history to that profile.
conflicts.reason: The profile is built from cookie information and linked to personal information, while the cookie section says cookie use is never linked to personal information. No exception or scope difference separates them.

conflicts.permit: We allow third parties, including business partners, advertising networks, and other advertising service providers, to collect information about your online activities through cookies, pixels, local storage, and other technologies to provide you interest based advertising.
conflicts.prohibit: These third party vendors and service providers only collect information about your use of our Platform in order to support us in providing you the Services.
conflicts.situation: An advertising service provider used by Amwell collects a user's online activity through cookies on the Platform to serve interest-based ads.
conflicts.reason: Advertising service providers are service providers, which the policy limits to collecting Platform use data to support the Services. The next sentence lets them collect broader online activity for interest-based advertising, with no stated precedence.

conflicts.permit: Hothead does not knowingly collect personal information from children under 16 without appropriate parental notice and consent.
conflicts.prohibit: No one under age 16 may provide any personal information to Hothead.
conflicts.situation: A 15-year-old user whose parent has given notice and consent submits a name and email address to Hothead through a game.
conflicts.reason: One statement implies Hothead collects from under-16 users with parental consent. The other says no one under 16 may provide any personal information. The policy does not say which governs.

conflicts.permit: These tools place persistent cookies in your browser to identify you as a unique user the next time you visit our website.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not use cookies for tracking purposes.
conflicts.situation: A returning website visitor's browser holds a persistent analytics cookie that identifies them as a unique user and records pages visited and time spent.
conflicts.reason: Persistent cookies that recognize returning users and record their navigation are tracking in the ordinary sense. The policy does not define tracking or exempt analytics cookies from the no-tracking statement.

conflicts.permit: Monitor third-party email services for compliance, when used.
conflicts.prohibit: The Personally Identifiable Information you provide us is not sold, traded, or otherwise transferred to outside parties.
conflicts.situation: The company sends marketing email to an address a user submitted through a website form, using a third-party email service.
conflicts.reason: Using a third-party email service transfers submitted email addresses to an outside party. The third-party disclosure section states no exception for service providers, and the policy does not say which statement governs.

conflicts.permit: Among the types of Personal Data that this Application collects, by itself or through third parties, there are: Cookies and Usage Data.
conflicts.prohibit: We DO NOT collect, store or use any personal information while you visit, download or upgrade our products.
conflicts.situation: A user plays 2048, and the Application records usage data such as IP address, device details, and pages visited.
conflicts.reason: The policy defines Cookies and Usage Data as Personal Data and says the Application collects them by itself, while the summary denies collecting any personal information. No scope or exception separates them.

conflicts.permit: For operation and maintenance purposes, this Application and any third party services may collect files that record interaction with this Application (System logs) or use for this purpose other Personal Data (such as IP Address).
conflicts.prohibit: We DO NOT collect, store or use any personal information while you visit, download or upgrade our products.
conflicts.situation: The 2048 Application records system logs of a user's interaction and uses the user's IP address for maintenance.
conflicts.reason: The system log section permits the Application itself to collect interaction records and use IP addresses, which the policy calls Personal Data. The summary denies any collection or use of personal information.

conflicts.prohibit: We require these entities not to use your information for any other purpose.
conflicts.situation: A WooPlus service provider handling email origination receives user personal information and uses it for a purpose its own privacy policy allows.
conflicts.reason: Service providers are barred from other uses, yet the next sentence lets any recipient use shared data under its own privacy policy, which WooPlus does not control. The policy does not say which governs.

conflicts.permit: Some of the third-party monetization SDKs integrated in our app may access your information for the purpose of ad optimization.
conflicts.prohibit: We never share your information with third parties.
conflicts.situation: A monetization SDK in the keyboard app reads the user's advertising ID, location, and IP address for ad optimization.
conflicts.reason: The app embeds third-party SDKs that obtain user information, while the sharing section says information is never shared with third parties. The policy states no exception for SDK partners.

conflicts.permit: These third-party SDKs may also collect your information such as GAID (Google Advertising ID on Android devices) or IDFA (Identifier for Advertising on iOS devices), region (defined as the location where a given language is used), location information and IP address.
conflicts.prohibit: The information will not be disclosed to any third parties.
conflicts.situation: An analytics SDK such as AppsFlyer in the keyboard app collects the user's advertising ID, location, and IP address.
conflicts.reason: Embedded analytics SDKs obtain identifiers and location from the app, while the policy says collected information will not be disclosed to any third parties. No exception for analytics providers is stated.

conflicts.permit: We may also share your Personal Information without your consent with Government agencies or other authorized law enforcement agencies (LEAs) mandated under law to obtain such information for the purpose of verification of identity or for prevention, detection, investigation including but not limited to cyber incidents, prosecution, and punishment of offences.
conflicts.prohibit: We may transfer your personal information or other information collected, stored, processed by us to any other entity or organization located in India or outside India only in to fulfil the terms of a contract we have with you or if you have consented (at the time of collection of information) to the same.
conflicts.situation: A law enforcement agency mandated under law requests a subscriber's identity details, and Airtel shares them without the subscriber's consent and outside any contract term.
conflicts.reason: The transfer clause limits transfers to any other entity to contract fulfilment or consent, while the government clause allows sharing without consent. Neither clause refers to the other as an exception.
